In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
thyroid function tests, especially TSH concentration, can be used as a predictive marker in the risk stratification of thyroid cancer.
the preoperative serum T4, TSH, and TgAb levels are not useful in predicting the risk of thyroid malignancy in patients undergoing thyroid surgery for nodular thyroid disease.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
thyroid function, autoantibody, and ultrasonography are important for predicting the risk of malignancies in patients with NODULAR THYROID DISEASE.
the preoperative serum TgAb concentration is not an independent predictor for thyroid cancer.
TSH, age, and sonographic features are important factors to predict the malignancy risk of thyroid nodules.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the TSH level can be used as a predictive marker for the presence of thyroid cancer in patients with thyroid nodular disease.
the preoperative TSH level can be used to stratify the risk of malignancies in patients with NTT.
the TSH concentration can be used as a marker for predicting the malignancy of NTD.
